content: Norovirus is an extremely contagious virus responsible for approximately 50% of gastroenteritis outbreaks globally. To prevent and control a norovirus outbreak, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends specific strategies. Management of a norovirus outbreak involves following a structured approach as outlined by the CDC. Diagnostic tools such as Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) are commonly used to confirm the presence of the virus. In cases of acute gastroenteritis, initial management should follow a systematic approach. This may include conducting a Complete Blood Count (CBC) and implementing Oral Replacement Therapy (ORT) to address dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. Recommended Actions (Do's): Suspect a norovirus outbreak when stool or vomitus samples from two or more patients test positive for norovirus using diagnostic methods such as RT-PCR, Enzyme Immunoassay (EIA), or electron microscopy. Actions to Avoid (Don'ts): Do not collect serum samples for routine detection of norovirus, as this is not a standard diagnostic method. Do not rely on hand sanitizers as a substitute for proper handwashing with soap and water, as handwashing is more effective in removing the virus.
